name: miadi-chronicle-episode-kit
description:
Creates, adopts, registers, works in, and closes Miadi Chronicle episodes — and refuses the one move that breaks them. The skill is the single kit-root copy at skills/chronicle-episode, linked in rather than duplicated, so this plugin and every other harness read the same file. A PreToolUse hook on Bash blocks a command that would mint an episode vessel by hand under $MIADI_CHRONICLE_ROOT and hands back the mkepisode invocation instead.

Use it for: minting an episode, adopting a manifest-less directory, checking an episode's five stages, registering into the medicine wheel, or any moment a chronicle path is about to be created.

<example>
Context: A new episode is needed for today's work
user: "start episode 334 for the distribution work"
assistant: "Running mkepisode with the reference and --register, then reading the receipt back before I claim it exists."
<commentary>
The vessel, the manifest and the wheel card are three separate facts. mkepisode writes all three and a .mw-registration.json receipt; the skill's gate is what stops a later stage being reported before it is proven.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: An agent reaches for mkdir inside the chronicle
assistant: (Bash) "mkdir -p $MIADI_CHRONICLE_ROOT/2026-09-04-episode-334-…"
assistant: (PreToolUse hook) "Refused: episode vessels are born by mkepisode, never mkdir."
<commentary>
63 of 172 episode directories carry no episode.yaml. They resolve by number, register on the wheel, return 200 — and stay invisible to lineage and to /chronicle, both of which read the manifest. Guidance against this has stood for months and the count rose, so this lane refuses instead of advising.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: A directory already holds finished work but has no manifest
user: "this episode folder was made by hand last week, fix it"
assistant: "mkepisode --adopt writes the missing episode.yaml beside the existing content, keeping the directory's own date, number and slug — with --status saying what the work actually is rather than stamping it a fresh vessel."
<commentary>
Adoption is the repair path and it is not the same as starting over. It changes nothing that was already there.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: Someone asks whether an episode is done
user: "/episode-status 333"
assistant: "Reading the five stages, each against its own proof — directory, manifest, commit, wheel card, receipt — and naming which are unproven rather than assumed."
<commentary>
The wheel returning 200 is evidence about the wheel, not about the manifest. A status that cannot tell those apart launders a guess into a guarantee.
</commentary>
</example>
